spec.title: Durable user PATH on native Windows (PROP-019 §2.6) — HKCU without the GUI, consent, REG_EXPAND_SZ, idempotence

p.purpose: **Purpose.** On Linux the Windows persister's logic runs against an in-memory user registry (`crates/vibe-cli/src/commands/vvm/env_registry_tests.rs`, `env_path_fix_tests.rs`): prepend the shim directory, dedupe case-insensitively, keep `%USERPROFILE%`-style text unexpanded, keep the value kind, write nothing when already canonical. What no fixture reaches is the real `HKCU\Environment` written through `RegSetValueExW`, the `WM_SETTINGCHANGE` broadcast that lets a terminal opened from Explorer see the change without logging off, and a corporate desktop where neither the Environment Variables dialog nor PowerShell is available. The owner proves these here, on a real Windows machine, before a release that ships the corporate-env campaign (`campaigns/corporate-env-2026-11/PLAN.md` §3.5, Phase 8).

p.isolation-note: The test edits the operator's real `HKCU\Environment\Path`. Step 0 exports it and the last step imports it back. Every command runs in `cmd.exe`, because PowerShell is commonly blocked on the machines this protects; `reg.exe` is used only by the operator to set up and observe, never by vibe.

facts.PRE-HOST: Windows 10/11 x86_64, a standard (non-administrator) user. Best: a managed desktop where the user cannot open the Environment Variables dialog (`rundll32 sysdm.cpl,EditEnvironmentVariables` is refused) and PowerShell is blocked. Without one, simulate in a test account with the local policy *User Configuration → Administrative Templates → Control Panel → Prohibit access to Control Panel and PC settings* and a software-restriction rule for `powershell.exe` / `pwsh.exe`.
facts.PRE-BINARIES: `vibe.exe` built from the revision under test (`cargo build -p vibe-cli --bins`, or the release archive), imported as a managed instance so the store and the stable shims exist: `vibe.exe self import --use`. Its shim directory is the `shim_dir` field of `vibe self doctor --json`; below it is written `%SHIMS%`.
facts.PRE-PROCMON: Optional: Sysinternals Process Monitor with a *Process Create* filter on parent `vibe.exe`, to observe that no child process is started.

section.title: Setup
section.fence: reg export HKCU\Environment "%TEMP%\mt07-env-backup.reg" /y vibe self doctor --json set SHIMS=<the shim_dir value printed above> reg add HKCU\Environment /v Path /t REG_EXPAND_SZ /d "^%USERPROFILE^%\mt07-marker;C:\Tools" /f reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path

p.EXP-SETUP: **Expected.** The query shows `Path REG_EXPAND_SZ %USERPROFILE%\mt07-marker;C:\Tools` with the `%USERPROFILE%` text literal (the carets kept `cmd.exe` from expanding it). The Environment Variables dialog cannot be opened on this desktop.

section.title: Steps

p.EXP-1: **Expected.** `durable_environment.target_kind` is `windows_registry`, `target` is `HKCU\Environment\Path`, `observation` is `present`, `path_entry` is `different` (the shim directory is not the first entry). Nothing is written: `reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path` is unchanged.

section.fence: vibe --unattended self doctor --fix --json reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path

p.EXP-2: **Expected.** The repair is refused (unattended mode alone is not consent; the message names `--yes`) and the registry value is byte-identical to the setup.

section.fence: vibe self doctor --fix --yes --json reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path > "%TEMP%\mt07-after-1.txt" type "%TEMP%\mt07-after-1.txt"

p.EXP-3: **Expected.** `fixed` is `true` and `durable_environment.path_entry` is `correct`. The value reads `%SHIMS%;%USERPROFILE%\mt07-marker;C:\Tools`: the shim directory first, the `%USERPROFILE%` entry still unexpanded text, the kind still `REG_EXPAND_SZ`. Process Monitor (if used) records no process created by `vibe.exe` — no `setx`, `reg`, `cmd` or PowerShell.

facts.STEP-4-NEW-TERMINAL: **A new terminal sees vibe without logging off.** Open a new `cmd.exe` from the Start menu or Win+R (both started by Explorer, which received `WM_SETTINGCHANGE`).

p.EXP-4: **Expected.** `where vibe` lists `%SHIMS%\vibe.exe` first; `vibe --version` prints the version under test; the process PATH carries the expanded `C:\Users\…\mt07-marker` entry, which proves the value was stored as `REG_EXPAND_SZ`. The terminal that ran step 3 keeps its old PATH, as the doctor's `process_path_refresh_needed` said.

section.fence: vibe self doctor --fix --yes --json reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path > "%TEMP%\mt07-after-2.txt" fc "%TEMP%\mt07-after-1.txt" "%TEMP%\mt07-after-2.txt"

p.EXP-5: **Expected.** `fc` reports no differences: the second run finds the value canonical and writes nothing.

facts.STEP-6-DEDUPE: **A differently spelled duplicate is folded.** Append the shim directory in upper case with a trailing backslash, then repair.

section.fence: reg add HKCU\Environment /v Path /t REG_EXPAND_SZ /d "^%USERPROFILE^%\mt07-marker;C:\Tools;<%SHIMS% in upper case>\" /f vibe self doctor --fix --yes --json reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path

p.EXP-6: **Expected.** The value is again `%SHIMS%;%USERPROFILE%\mt07-marker;C:\Tools`: the shim directory appears exactly once, first; the other entries keep their bytes and order.

section.fence: reg add HKCU\Environment /v Path /t REG_SZ /d "C:\Tools" /f vibe self doctor --fix --yes --json reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path

facts.STEP-8-APPLY: **`vibe self apply` with the PATH question (Phase 8).** Reset the value as in the setup, then with a site profile `corp.toml` (any valid profile; `[path]` absent):

section.fence: vibe --unattended self apply corp.toml --json vibe self apply corp.toml vibe --unattended self apply corp.toml --fix-path --json reg query HKCU\Environment /v Path

p.EXP-8: **Expected.** The unattended run without `--fix-path` leaves the value untouched and reports the PATH fix as `skipped` with reason `not_interactive` and a hint naming `--fix-path`. The attended run asks whether to put `%SHIMS%` on PATH at `HKCU\Environment\Path` with **Yes** preselected; Enter applies it (`applied`, consent `interactive`). After resetting the value again, the unattended `--fix-path` run applies it with consent `flag`. In every applied case the value, kind and new-terminal behaviour match steps 3–5.

p.pass-criteria: On a desktop without the Environment Variables dialog or PowerShell, vibe puts its shim directory first on the user PATH only with consent, through the registry API and no child process; a new terminal started from Explorer finds `vibe`; `%USERPROFILE%` text and the `REG_EXPAND_SZ` kind survive; a re-run changes nothing; a duplicate is folded. Step 8 joins the criteria once `vibe self apply` lands. The owner signs the date below.
